name: live_right_side_not_null_becomes_nullable
description: LEFT JOIN makes right-side NOT NULL columns nullable, verified against a live engine rather than just the analyzer
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE users (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
CREATE TABLE orders (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), total NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now())
query_sql:
-- @name GetUsersWithOrderTotals
-- @returns :many
SELECT u.id, o.total, o.created_at AS order_created_at FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id ORDER BY u.id

columns.name: total
columns.note: NOT NULL in schema but nullable due to LEFT JOIN

columns.name: order_created_at
columns.note: NOT NULL in schema but nullable due to LEFT JOIN

sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc marks o.total and o.created_at as non-nullable because both are NOT NULL in the schema, ignoring the LEFT JOIN
sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe correctly infers that all right-side columns of a LEFT JOIN become nullable, and this fixture also proves it against six live engines rather than the analyzer alone
